posts.title: What Is a Computer, Really?

slides.headline: What is a computer?
slides.text: At its core, a computer is just a machine that takes input, processes it, and produces output.
slides.descriptionVisual: Simple 3-box flow: Input → Process → Output. Context: Hook / Open — high-impact, text-only. A bold question or statement to stop the scroll. Style: Tech Blue color palette (primary #1E5FA8, accent #A9D0F5), vertical 1080x1350 social slide canvas, clean line-art icon/diagram style, uniform stroke width.

slides.headline: Analog vs digital
slides.text: Analog is continuous, like a clock hand sweeping smoothly. Digital is discrete, like a light switch that's only on or off.
slides.descriptionVisual: Split screen: clock hand (left) vs light switch (right). Context: Comparison — split-screen, two columns, contrasting colors, one differentiator icon per side. slides.text: Computers turn electricity into information — high voltage means one thing, low voltage means another.
slides.descriptionVisual: Wire icon with glowing pulse representing voltage highs/lows. Context: Process / Flow — step-by-step visual with arrows, left-to-right or top-to-bottom. slides.headline: Why computers use 0 and 1
slides.text: Computers use just two states, 0 and 1, because it's far easier to reliably detect 'on' or 'off' than many in-between levels.
